= camel cmd chaos-explore

Let there be chaos: an AI explores by itself how a running integration copes with faults, for a time budget, and reports what held and what broke


== Usage

[source,bash]
----
camel cmd chaos-explore [options]
----



== Options

[cols="2,5,1,2",options="header"]
|===
| Option | Description | Default | Type
| `--api-key` | API key. Also reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, WATSONX_APIKEY, or LLM_API_KEY env vars |  | String
| `--api-type` | API type: 'ollama', 'openai', 'anthropic', or 'watsonx' |  | ApiType
| `--budget` | How long the AI explores, between 10s and 2h | 10m | String
| `--focus` | What to explore, such as a route id (default: all routes) |  | String
| `--max-iterations` | Maximum number of tool-calling rounds | 100 | int
| `--model` | Model to use. Default: the provider's default; with Ollama the installed model best at tool calling |  | String
| `--save` | Save the report in test/chaos/reports (as markdown, and the journal as JSON), and each experiment that failed as a scenario in test/chaos, to replay it | true | boolean
| `--show-tools` | Show the tool calls and results as they happen |  | boolean
| `--timeout` | Timeout in seconds for one answer of the LLM (an experiment can take minutes) | 300 | int
| `--tools` | The tools the model gets: core (a small set, for a local model), full, or auto | auto | ToolSet
| `--url` | LLM API endpoint URL, as for camel ask. Auto-detected if not specified |  | String
| `--verbose` | Print debug information of the LLM calls |  | boolean
| `--yes` | Let the AI send messages to endpoints the integration does not have, and run the other calls that camel ask asks for first, without asking |  | boolean
| `-h,--help` | Display the help and sub-commands |  | boolean
|===
